lines: {target}? Sound travels farther than sense.
If anyone heads for Deep Dark, tell them. Walk soft and do not open every chest.
Sculk hears what pride forgets.
I had the wrong picture of Deep Dark. Your version makes more sense.
I'll remember Deep Dark as darkness that listens back.
One safe room at Deep Dark is worth more than five hurried walls.
I would brace the side nearest the sculk-lined passages before anyone settled in.
I would keep the first shelter at Deep Dark simple until we understood the site.
If we had to run, the torch-marked path leading upward should already be marked and open.
At Deep Dark, everyone should recognize the start of the torch-marked path leading upward before the group spreads out.
Anything valuable at Deep Dark can wait until the return route is safe.
At Deep Dark, a shelter plan that ignores unseen drops beyond the torchlight is not finished.
When the danger at Deep Dark comes from unseen drops beyond the torchlight, the nearest solid corner will matter.
While moving through Deep Dark, I would keep one hand free and remember unseen drops beyond the torchlight.
I would note every narrow point along the torch-marked path leading upward at Deep Dark. Tired feet find those places.
The shape of the torch-marked path leading upward matters as much as its length.
At Deep Dark, one loose block can explain a whole ruined wall.
At Deep Dark, nobody should carry a full load over the sculk-lined passages until one person tests the footing.
I would rather return empty-handed from Deep Dark than leave someone alone near the sculk-lined passages.
A missing tool is annoying. A missing traveler at Deep Dark is worse.
{target}? Stone teeth hang above and wait below.
If anyone heads for Dripstone Caves, tell them. Look up as often as you look down.
Pointed stone makes every stumble serious.
If I ever reach Dripstone Caves, your story will be in my head.
I will remember Dripstone Caves as a cave that bites from both directions.
For Dripstone Caves, I would carry rubble for fill and dressed stone for the places taking weight.
If we camped at Dripstone Caves, I would put the entrance where the torch-marked path leading upward stayed visible.
Stone for Dripstone Caves needs rough faces for grip, not polished faces for show.
I would keep spare blocks beside the torch-marked path leading upward, not buried at the bottom of a pack.
If we had to run, the torch-marked path leading upward should already be marked and open.
I would count the turns back from Dripstone Caves while my legs were still fresh.
With unseen drops beyond the torchlight ahead, I would keep the group close at Dripstone Caves.
No bit of loot at Dripstone Caves is worth letting unseen drops beyond the torchlight catch us unprepared.
A warning about unseen drops beyond the torchlight belongs at the first marker, not the last one.
I would tap the solid surfaces at Dripstone Caves and leave the hollow ones alone.
I would note every narrow point along the torch-marked path leading upward at Dripstone Caves. Tired feet find those places.
At Dripstone Caves, I would watch where loose pieces gather near the dripstone passages. They show where people slip.
Do not split up at Dripstone Caves just because the ground looks open.
Before dark at Dripstone Caves, I would choose one meeting point and make it obvious.
At Dripstone Caves, keep the group within calling distance when cave darkness makes it hard to see.
{target}? Pretty caves still have long drops.
If anyone heads for Lush Caves, tell them. Watch the vines and the holes between them.
Glow berries light paths that may not be safe.
I know more about Lush Caves now than I did this morning.
I will remember Lush Caves as a cave trying very hard to look harmless.
Any shelter at Lush Caves should be easy to find and even easier to leave.
Good corners matter more than decoration when building near the lush cave floor.
I would save the straightest blocks for the shelter corners at Lush Caves.
I would count the turns back from Lush Caves while my legs were still fresh.
If the light changed, I would still want the torch-marked path leading upward easy to recognize.
I would place pale blocks along the torch-marked path leading upward so nobody had to guess on the way back.
I would turn back from Lush Caves before unseen drops beyond the torchlight became harder to manage.
I would choose the shelter site at Lush Caves with unseen drops beyond the torchlight in mind.
If our plan did not account for unseen drops beyond the torchlight, I would call it unfinished.
At Lush Caves, I would watch where debris collected before choosing a place to stand.
I would look for old repairs at Lush Caves. They show what failed before we arrived.
At Lush Caves, I would watch where loose pieces gather near the lush cave floor. They show where people slip.
I would spend the first hour at Lush Caves making the way back easier.
At Lush Caves, we can stop for stories after we check the torch-marked path leading upward and secure the shelter.
At Lush Caves, the last person in line should know the plan as well as the first.
